source.title: D-Scope: Decomposing and Steering Diffusion Transformers with Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Xinyue Xu; Jiahao Zhang; Li-Jie Hu; Peter Hase; Hao Wang

page_placements.theme: Reconstruction and proxy metrics do not establish semantic recovery

record.tranche_reason: The study uses SAE features and decoder directions as tools for steering diffusion-transformer generation, but does not test superposition, feature competition, polysemanticity, or the geometry of overlapping features.
record.gate_note: The paper reports controlled effects of adding retrieved SAE decoder directions, but these interventions do not test whether features are naturally superposed or what dimensionality their underlying representations have. Results cited from other studies are background only. The reported steering averages are recorded below; unrelated style-suppression and nudity-readout experiments are not included.
record.test_reason: The study uses SAE decoder directions from diffusion transformers (SANA-Sprint, Nitro-1-PixArt, SANA teacher) as steering tools. It reports only its own retrieval-and-steering method's performance (Region SigLIP Δ, LPIPS-out) and dictionary-quality diagnostics. It does not test overlapping feature geometry, capacity pressure, polysemanticity mechanisms, feature spread in LLMs, the stability or canonicity of SAE features, or feature dimensionality. Every SAE is trained with a single seed, and no cross-seed or cross-width comparison is made.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also conclude that a single retrieved direction reaches up to 86% of the Oracle Dense target gain. They add that a larger feature pool does not guarantee stronger steering, so selecting effective directions matters.
record.recipe_differences: The study trains and evaluates SAEs on diffusion-transformer activations, retrieves features through SigLIP visual centroids, and intervenes with decoder directions. It does not reproduce the original toy-network superposition experiments or measure their overlap geometry.
record.method_sensitivity: Steering results vary with generator environment, retrieval strategy, SAE family, and input-processing setting. Contrastive retrieval raises mean target gain across all 45 matched dictionary and generator comparisons, while preservation effects vary by generator.

fits_no_version.finding: A single retrieved SAE decoder direction yields positive regional target gains under masked, best-of-sweep steering. It reaches up to 86% of the Oracle Dense gain.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In diffusion transformers, text-retrieved SAE decoder directions can drive localized generation edits; target alignment and outside-region preservation are separate outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: Across 150 DiT SAEs, high reconstruction EV coexists with low dictionary utilization and low visual-evidence coverage. For example, uncentered TopK at Nitro layer 2 has EV 0.9997 but 1.5% utilization (Table 5). Centering raises utilization.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE reconstruction fidelity does not indicate how many dictionary features are used or interpretable; dictionary contents depend on training choices such as centering and SAE family.

record.problems: The study does not directly test any listed superposition claim. Steering effects are deliberately induced by decoder-direction interventions and are not evidence that the corresponding behavior arises without intervention. Benchmark steering uses per-case best-of-sweep strength selection and three generation seeds; the reported retrieval averages do not state uncertainty.
record.rows_left_out: No additional results relevant to the listed versions were left out. Style suppression and nudity-readout results concern separate applications rather than superposition or the geometry of SAE features.

untested.parts: Toy overcomplete networks, sparsity-dependent transition, overlap geometry: none tested.
Capacity competition and dedicated versus shared dimensions: not tested.
Alternative causes of polysemanticity: not tested.
The study uses diffusion transformers, not LLMs. SAEs are fit, but distributed-neuron representation is not measured.
Completeness, stability across seeds, and canonicity of SAE features: not tested. Only one training seed is used per configuration.
The study applies single decoder directions but does not compare 1-D with multi-dimensional features.

record.verdict_notes: The style-suppression and nudity-readout appendices also use SAE features as tools and test no version. The dictionary-quality analysis is relevant to SAE evaluation generally but does not address the completeness or canonicity in V5.

versions.untested_parts: No test of overcomplete toy networks, feature sparsity, overlap geometry, sparsity-dependent transitions, or regular geometric structure.
No test of capacity pressure as an explanation for polysemanticity or of dedicated versus shared dimensions.
No test of polysemanticity or of alternative mechanisms producing it.
The study evaluates diffusion transformers, not LLMs, and does not measure feature spread across neurons in LLMs.

The study assesses whether selected SAE directions can be retrieved and used for controlled edits, but does not test whether SAE features are complete, canonical, or stable units of the representation.
It applies individual decoder directions but does not test whether represented features are intrinsically one-dimensional or compare them with multidimensional features.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: SAE features and decoder directions serve as tools for retrieval, steering, suppression and readout, without testing superposition or the completeness, stability or canonicality of SAE units.

tranche.reason: The study evaluates SAE dictionary diagnostics and retrieval-based steering in diffusion transformers; these results do not directly test the listed claim versions.

source_check.notes: Section 4.2 and Table 5 confirm EV 0.9997 and utilization 1.5% for uncentered TopK at Nitro layer 2. Utilization measures activity during the preceding 256,000 training tokens, not held-out feature activity.
